observations.explanation: The paper describes retrieval-on-demand, relevance/support/usefulness critique tokens, and inference-time control through segment-level beam search (pp. 3–6). Its evaluations span six tasks, including reasoning and long-form generation (pp. 7–8).

Table 2 reports six task settings and varied metrics, and the authors state SELF-RAG has the best performance among non-proprietary LM-based models on all tasks, while noting proprietary-model exceptions on particular metrics (p. 8).

The ablation results compare training and inference components, including removing the critic and using the top passage regardless of relevance (p. 9). The inference analyses vary support-token weights and retrieval thresholds, reporting effects on citation precision, MAUVE, retrieval frequency, and accuracy rather than claiming one setting is universally best (pp. 9–10).

The authors explicitly acknowledge that outputs may not be fully supported by citations (p. 11). The human evaluation sampled 50 PopQA and biography-generation cases (p. 10), and the appendix includes examples where predictions are unsupported or only partially supported (p. 24).
